paragraphs.en: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to "put everything out," he recalled. But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona's Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent. Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.
paragraphs.zh: 汤姆·斯韦特纳姆回忆说，20世纪70年代他加入美国林务局时，接到的指令是‘把所有火都扑灭’。但后来，他进入亚利桑那大学树木年轮研究实验室攻读研究生时，却惊讶地发现，在欧洲殖民者抵达这片大陆之前的数百年间，就已经存在反复发生火灾的记录。他分析的一些树木的年轮中，留下了20多处火烧伤痕。

paragraphs.en: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn't have been severe enough to kill most trees. Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier. They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease. Because flammable material couldn't build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.
paragraphs.zh: 火灾如此频繁地发生，意味着它们不可能严重到足以杀死大多数树木。相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁发生的低烈度火灾会使许多生态系统更加健康。它们清除了森林中的死树和病树，减少了竞争，也抑制了疾病传播。由于可燃物无法在林地中堆积，火势往往蔓延缓慢，并在到达此前烧过的区域时逐渐熄灭。

paragraphs.en: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent. Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month. In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall. The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.
paragraphs.zh: 2022年，斯韦特纳姆与其他科学家合作，建立了一个汇集北美大陆各地带有火烧伤痕的树木的数据库。他们建立的北美树木年轮火烧伤痕网络（NAFSN），为上个月发表的一项研究提供了基础。在这项研究中，研究人员将历史上的火灾发生频率与过去几十年记录的野火进行比较，发现火灾数量出现了显著的不足。NAFSN各研究地点实际发生的火灾数量，还不到在没有人为灭火的情况下预计会发生数量的四分之一。

paragraphs.en: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire. "Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions."
paragraphs.zh: 国际荒野火灾协会前主席凯莉·马丁表示，这种不足证明了现代灭火工作的成效。‘然而，灭火与气候变化共同造成的后果，已经削弱了人类扑灭火灾的能力，尤其是扑灭那些在最危险的天气条件下燃起的火灾的能力。’

paragraphs.en: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it. At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient. These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park's facilities. Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 马丁说，为了防止整个生态系统付之一炬，人们必须让有益于生态的火重新回到需要它的地方。在约塞米蒂国家公园，马丁曾负责监督实施一种被称为计划烧除的措施，以增强当地生态环境的恢复能力。这些火经过精心规划，在天气条件使火势易于控制的时期人为点燃，帮助清除这座重要公园的设施周围积聚的部分可燃物。研究表明，这些计划烧除能够降低后续野火的烈度，即便后来发生的火灾遇上最危险的天气条件也是如此。

paragraphs.en: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said. "It's a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging," said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，专家表示，尽管科学家和政府官员越来越认同森林中需要更多火，但气候变化正使这一策略的实施更加困难。华盛顿大学火灾生态学家苏珊·普里查德说：‘这是一把双刃剑，因为在气候变化的影响下，野火变得更猛烈、规模更大，我们也就更加需要开展这项工作，但与此同时，这项工作也变得更加困难。’
